newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay blue chips erase week's gains, finish lower.
newsitem.headline: Bombay blue chips erase week's gains, finish lower.

text.p: Bombay shares finished lower on Thursday as punters wiped out previous gains, pulling the benchmark index 1.8 percent lower, traders said.
"Yesterday the operators took the market up and now we're back to square one," said a trader at a foreign fund.
The 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) fell 61.30 points or 1.8 percent to a provisional close of 3352.71, erasing gains made in the previous session.
On Wednesday the index jumped 66.64 points to 3414.01 as Calcutta operators covered short positions on the last day of the account. The rise was aided by a technical correction.
"Yesterday's gains were completely given up today on higher volumes as speculators used the rise to unload a lot of stock," another trader said.
Traders said fresh demand was restricted to select pivotals with funds on the lookout for bargains.
Shares of Oriental Bank of Commerce fell 6.65 to 69.85 on the NSE and shed 6.50 rupees to 69.50 on the BSE as funds sold.
A banking analyst at a foreign brokerage said a change in an accounting rule would result in a one-time additional tax charge of some 520 million rupees for Oriental Bank in 1996/97 (April-March).
"Despite this tax burden we expect some profit growth in 1996/97," the analyst said.
He said there were also rumours in the market that the bank was facing difficulties with recoveries in India's most populous state of Uttar Pradesh.
Finance firm ICICI said at an annual meeting its loan disbursements rose more than 30 percent in the first few months of 1996/97 (April-March). The firm did not specify the months.
